title: Lingering hazard
subtitle: Build a readable lingering hazard with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
summary: An attack leaves danger active after the initial hit.
overview: An attack leaves danger active after the initial hit, converting a momentary threat into temporary arena control and future route planning.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a lingering hazard as one rule.

demo.title: Test the lingering hazard
phaseDescriptions: Distinguish the initial impact, active hazard, and expiration states so the player knows when entering the area is unsafe and when it clears.
Players route around the zone, bait it toward low-value space, remove it with a supported tool, or accept a clearly priced tradeoff.
The zone cools, shrinks, or fades through an unmistakable expiration state before its space becomes safe again.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Distinguish the initial impact, active hazard, and expiration states so the player knows when entering the area is unsafe and when it clears.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: Players route around the zone, bait it toward low-value space, remove it with a supported tool, or accept a clearly priced tradeoff.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: The zone cools, shrinks, or fades through an unmistakable expiration state before its space becomes safe again.

mistakes.title: Hazards that outlive their readable visuals create invisible damage and make the arena state impossible to audit
mistakes.body: Hazards that outlive their readable visuals create invisible damage and make the arena state impossible to audit.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible lingering hazard cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Tune footprint, lifetime, placement frequency, damage cadence, and maximum simultaneous coverage as one arena budget.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Let zones grow, drift, or react to other attacks while enforcing a cap that preserves at least one viable route.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: The zone cools, shrinks, or fades through an unmistakable expiration state before its space becomes safe again.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: An attack leaves danger active after the initial hit, converting a momentary threat into temporary arena control and future route planning. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: Players route around the zone, bait it toward low-value space, remove it with a supported tool, or accept a clearly priced tradeoff. Tune footprint, lifetime, placement frequency, damage cadence, and maximum simultaneous coverage as one arena budget.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: Hazards that outlive their readable visuals create invisible damage and make the arena state impossible to audit. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The signal must reveal the relevant timing and geometry before commitment.
The complete player extent and the active region determine whether the route is real.
The response uses an ordinary supported verb and produces an observable result.
At least one route remains reachable with the movement options available at this point.
